production_norm_layout_audit.json.interpretation: CPU layout/contract diagnostic only; no GPU run or production claim is represented.

comparison.causality_limit: Different layout and reduction grouping are concrete differences consistent with a changed reduction result, but static artifacts do not prove this is the sole cause of layer-2 Q/scale divergence.
comparison.layout_difference: Production failure is sizePerThread=[1,4], threadsPerWarp=[1,32], warpsPerCTA=[1,16] (one row, four reduction elements per lane, 512 threads per CTA). S1 reference is sizePerThread=[1,8], threadsPerWarp=[1,32], warpsPerCTA=[1,8] (two rows, eight reduction elements per lane, 256 threads per CTA).
comparison.local_arithmetic_evidence: The saved production PTX uses two packed f32x2 square vectors per lane and its lane-local fold includes two fma.rn.f32x2 instructions followed by add.f32x2 before the warp butterfly. S1 exact-tree plan and reference PTX record eight consecutive values per lane with rounded(square1), fma(square0), fma(square2), rounded-add(square3), fma(square4), rounded-add(square5), fma(square6), rounded-add(square7). Thus lane grouping and the observed local fold differ; the exact scalar ordering of every production w16 lane term is unresolved in this CPU audit.
comparison.performance_limit: No NCU data were collected; no stall or performance-cause inference is made.
comparison.resource_comparability: Production child compiler JSON records shared=64 and omits register/spill counts; cuobjdump reports REG:26, STACK:0, SHARED:1024, LOCAL:0 for its cubin. S1 launcher metadata reports registers=37, spills=0, shared_bytes=64. These are preserved as source-specific raw measurements; the register/shared figures are not normalized across inspection methods.
comparison.tree_difference: The warp butterfly is 16,8,4,2,1 in both PTX files; the CTA cross-warp reduction differs in extent: production w16 uses a 16-partial shared reduction with offsets 8,4,2,1, while S1 w8 uses an 8-partial shared reduction with offsets 4,2,1.
